info.bio:
Scream fue una banda de hardcore punk y punk rock de Washington, D.C, que se mantuvo activa desde 1981 hasta 1990.
Scream se formó en el norte de Virginia en 1981. Estaba compuesto por el cantante Peter Stahl, su hermano y guitarrista Franz Stahl, el bajista Skeeter Thompson y el baterista Kent Stax.
Se considera a Scream una de las bandas referentes del movimiento hardcore en Washington, D.C.
Junto con bandas como Minor Threat y Government Issue

scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El punk como «violento, rápido y ruidoso» tarda en conquistar EE UU, pero cuando lo hace el hardcore se convierte durante dos décadas en el idioma nacional de millones de chavales. Misfits y el «scum-rock»; el crossover punk-metal (Suicidal Tendencies, Corrosion Of Conformity, Agnostic Front); Mission Of Burma en Boston. Washington: Bad Brains (reggae, funk y metal diez años por delante), Minor Threat (el «straight-edge») y Rites Of Spring, inventores del emo-core. San Francisco: Dead Kennedys de Jello Biafra, D.R.I. (thrash antes que Metallica), Flipper. Los «beach punks» de Los Ángeles: Germs, X, Black Flag (Damaged), Descendents, Gun Club (Fire Of Love), Bad Religion. El jazz-core de Minutemen y Saccharine Trust; en el Medio Oeste, Husker Du y Replacements cambian el hardcore para siempre; en Chicago, Naked Raygun y Big Black de Steve Albini; en Europa, The Ex y los italianos CCCP.

mentions.text: …melodic flair that the others lacked. Bleach (1989) was both rudimentary, savage and fragile. Nevermind (1991), featuring new drummer Dave Grohl (ex-Scream), increased the melodic factor, and found an even more unlikely balance between pathos and disgust, tenderness and rage, melancholy and rebellion.…

podcast.title: Drummer Audition (1987)
podcast.body: In 1987, Dave Grohl discovered a notice at a music store indicating Scream was seeking a new drummer. He contacted the band, auditioned, and secured the position, which he considered his "dream gig," by the end of that month, replacing their long-time drummer. "He tore the note down, contacted the band, auditioned, and got what he thought was his dream gig by the end of that month."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 1

podcast.title: Breakup Over "Girlfriend Troubles" (1990)
podcast.body: The band broke up in the summer of 1990 over "girlfriend troubles" while they were on tour. This left Dave Grohl stranded in Los Angeles, leading to the circumstances that eventually brought him to audition for Nirvana. "Scream had broken up over some girlfriend troubles while the band was on tour leaving Dave stranded in Los Angeles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 2

podcast.title: Lawsuit Against Dave Grohl (1990)
podcast.body: After Dave Grohl joined Nirvana and they signed a major label deal, someone associated with Scream sued him for $40,000. They claimed Dave was still under contract to them due to an agreement he had signed, despite the band having "long broken up." This legal issue highlighted the complexities of early career contracts. "When he joined Nirvana and they were signed to DGC, Dave was immediately sued by someone associated with Scream for $40,000 saying that he was still under contract to them, even though Scream had long broken up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 2

podcast.title: Mid-Tour Breakup (1990)
podcast.body: In September 1990, the band Scream broke up abruptly in the middle of a tour when their bass player unexpectedly left due to "girlfriend problems." This sudden dissolution left drummer Dave Grohl stranded in Los Angeles and actively seeking a new musical engagement, which ultimately led to his joining Nirvana. "Dave Girl was part of a group called Scream, but they broke up in September 1990 right in the middle of a tour when the bass player bailed because of girlfriend problems."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 5

podcast.title: Breakup and Dave Grohl's Next Step – Tour Interruption
podcast.body: Scream broke up in September 1990, during the middle of a tour, when their bass player unexpectedly left due to personal issues related to a girlfriend. This left Dave Grohl stranded in Los Angeles and led to him seeking a new band, eventually joining Nirvana. "Scream broke up in September 1990 right in the middle of a tour the bass player bolted because of some girlfriend problems Straining the band and Dave and Los Angeles."

podcast.body: Dave Grohl quit school at the age of 17 specifically to join this Washington D.C.-based band. This decision marked a significant turning point in his early musical career. "Dave quit school at age 17 to join a DC band called Scream."

podcast.title: First Extensive Touring
podcast.body: Joining Scream provided Dave Grohl with his first opportunities to tour extensively across America and, for the first time, in Europe (including Amsterdam), at ages 17 and 18, which he viewed as a liberating experience. "I'd never been past Chicago, and also, and I joined Scream. And we tour America. I think I was 18 or 17. We tour America, and it was just like, oh my God, I'd never been to California."

podcast.title: Local Legends (Pre-Grohl)
podcast.body: Before Dave Grohl joined in 1987, Scream was considered a legendary local DC hardcore group, having been active for approximately five years. "he became a fan of a local DC hardcore group called Scream. They were legends around town."

podcast.title: Underage Touring and Deception
podcast.body: When Dave Grohl joined Scream at age 17, he was underage to play in bars, so he lied about his age, claiming to be 22, to be able to tour and perform legally. "Dave was just 17 at the time, which meant he was under age when he came to playing at bars. So he lied. He said he was 22."

xref.title: Buzz Osborne's Recommendation to Nirvana (1990)
xref.body: Buzz Osborne, a member of The Melvins and a figure "idolized by Kurt Cobain," played a pivotal role in Dave Grohl joining Nirvana. Osborne recommended Dave for the open drummer slot after Scream broke up, directly leading to Dave's audition and subsequent entry into Nirvana. "But then Buzz Osborne of the Melvins, a guy idolized by Kurt Cobain, recommended him for the open drummer slot with Nirvana."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 2

xref.title: Dave Grohl Joined Nirvana Because His Band's Bassist Broke Up with His Girlfriend (1990)
xref.body: Dave dropped out of high school to tour with DC punk band Scream for about three years. In the summer of 1990, bassist Skeater Thompson flaked out mid-tour in Los Angeles over the loss of his girlfriend, canceling multiple shows. Dave was left penniless (temporarily crashing with three female mud wrestlers) and doing cash tiling work for food money. He called Melvins leader King Buzzo (Kurt Cobain's idol), whom he'd met in Europe, who told him Kurt had a band needing a drummer. Dave flew to Seattle on September 21, 1990; four days later he auditioned and passed. Dave later wrote a song about Skeater Thompson called "Just Another Story About Skeater Thompson," available only on a cassette-only release made under the name "Late" in late 1990, titled *Pocket Watch*. "Dave has never forgotten Skeater Thompson and how thankful he is that Skeater had such bad girlfriend trouble."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 10 Unusual Things About Nirvana

xref.title: Dave Grohl's Audition and Joining (1990)
xref.body: After his previous band Scream disbanded, Dave Grohl was connected with Nirvana through Buzz Osborne of The Melvins. Grohl auditioned at the Dutchman rehearsal space in Seattle on September 25, 1990, and secured the drumming position instantly, completing the lineup that would become one of the most successful rock bands of the 1990s. "He auditioned at the Dutchman rehearsal space in Seattle on September 25th, 1990, and he got the gig instantly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 5

xref.title: Harling Talks AD Alias (1990)
xref.body: In the summer of 1990, while still with Scream, Dave Grohl recorded new demos on his own, creating the alias "Harling Talks Angel Divine," or "Harling Talks AD" for short. With assistance from Barrett Jones and Toss Newyn Huizen, he recorded experimental material that he never expected to go anywhere, and there was never a "Harling Talks show." "Dave created a new alias, he called Harling Talks Angel Divine or Harling Talks AD for short."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 2

xref.title: Joining Nirvana (1990)
xref.body: A few months after recording his Harling Talks AD demos, Dave Grohl received a call to audition for Nirvana. Scream had broken up over "girlfriend troubles" while on tour, leaving Dave stranded in Los Angeles. Buzz Osborne of The Melvins, who was idolized by Kurt Cobain, recommended Dave for the open drummer position. Dave flew to Seattle, arriving on Friday, September 21, 1990, and after an informal audition, became a member of the band without any explicit invitation, simply because "they just didn't ask him to leave." "Dave packed his kit into a large cardboard box and boarded a flight for Seattle, arriving on Friday, September 21, 1990."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 2

xref.title: Post-Scream Legal Issue (1990)
xref.body: After joining Nirvana and the band signed to DGC, Dave Grohl was sued for $40,000 by someone associated with Scream. This legal action alleged that Dave was still under contract to Scream due to an agreement he signed at some point during his time with them, even though Scream had already broken up. Fortunately, Dave had lawyers who were able to deal with the situation. "Dave was immediately sued by someone associated with Scream for $40,000 saying that he was still under contract to them, even though Scream had long broken up."

xref.title: Devotional Tour Environment (1993-94)
xref.body: The Depeche Mode Devotional Tour in 1993-94 was marked by significant debauchery, particularly from Dave Gahan, which reportedly "scared straight" the opening act, Primal Scream. The tour environment was so intense that it featured both its own drug counselor and a drug dealer, alongside frequent run-ins with the police. "The tour had both its own drug counselor and drug dealer. There were run-ins with the cops."

xref.title: Murder in Seattle - July 7, 1993
xref.body: On July 7, 1993, Mia Zapata left the Comet Tavern in downtown Seattle around 1 AM, visited a friend, and then headed home with headphones on. Sometime within the next hour, she was beaten, raped, and murdered, found strangled with her hoodie cord at approximately 3:20 AM on the 100 block of 24th Avenue South. "On July 7th, 1993, Mia left a bar called the Comet Tavern in downtown Seattle. Sometime in the next 60 minutes she was beaten, raped and murdered. She had been strangled with a cord of her hoodie. A scream was heard at around 3 and then her body was found at about 320 on the 100 block of 24th Avenue South."

xref.title: Opening Act for Depeche Mode (1993)
xref.body: Primal Scream opened for Depeche Mode on their 1993 "Songs of Faith and Devotion" tour, where they were reportedly frightened by the severity of Dave Gahan's heroin addiction, indicating Gahan's drug use was extreme even by their standards. "His appetite for drugs was so great on the songs of Faith and Devotion Tour in 1993 that he even scared the guys in the opening act primal scream."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: RocknRoll Rehab

xref.title: Primal Scream's Shocking Experience (1993)
xref.body: Dave Gahan reportedly insisted that Primal Scream open for Depeche Mode on the Devotional Tour because he knew they enjoyed partying. However, Primal Scream was so appalled by the level of drug use and excess they witnessed that they allegedly gave up drugs entirely, despite their prior extensive use. "The story goes that primal scream was so shocked by what they saw that they gave up drugs entirely."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

xref.title: Shocked by Depeche Mode's Excess (1993)
xref.body: Primal Scream served as an opening act for Depeche Mode's Devotional Tour at Dave Gahan's insistence, as he believed they shared a similar partying spirit. However, the band was reportedly so shocked by the extreme drug use they witnessed that their singer, Bobby Gillespie, was quoted saying Dave Gahan did more drugs than all of Primal Scream combined, leading them to give up drugs entirely. "The story goes that primal scream was so shocked by what they saw that they gave up drugs entirely."

xref.title: Mani Death (2025) – Distinctive Bass Lines Sung by Audiences Before Vocals Entered
xref.body: Mani (Gary Mounfield), bassist of Stone Roses and Primal Scream, died in 2025. His bass lines on songs such as "I Wanna Be Adored" were so distinctive and immediately recognizable that audiences would sing them aloud before the vocals even entered. He was a key contributor to the "Madchester" sound. "His bass line in songs like 'I Wanna Be Adored' was so distinctive that the audience sang it before the voice entered."

xref.title: Big Break with Scream – Joining an Established Band
xref.body: Dave Grohl's significant career break occurred around 1987 when he was 18 years old. An established local band named Scream announced they were looking for a drummer, and Grohl applied for and secured the position. "Dave's big break came at about 1987 when an established local band called Scream let it be known that they were looking for a drummer So 18-year-old Dave applied and got the job."

xref.title: Dave Grohl's Entrance – A Desperate Call
xref.body: After his band Scream broke up mid-tour in September 1990, Dave Grohl was stranded in Los Angeles and desperate for a gig. He called his friend Buzz Osborne of The Melvins, hoping for news of drummer openings. Osborne gave Grohl Kurt Cobain's phone number, leading to an invitation to Seattle. Grohl packed his drums in a cardboard box and joined Nirvana. "So buzz gave Dave the bass player his phone number and Dave made the call and was invited to come on up Packed all his drums into a big cardboard box grabbed his only bag close and headed up the coast to join this weird little band called of course Nirvana."

xref.title: Departure from Dane Bramage
xref.body: He abruptly left his band Dane Bramage to join Scream, an offer he "couldn't refuse," which led to hard feelings within Dane Bramage and the band's dissolution. "that band died because Dave bailed. He got an offer that he just couldn't refuse."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 1

xref.title: Dropping Out of High School
xref.body: With his mother's blessing, he dropped out of high school to tour with Scream. His mother agreed on two conditions: he pay rent and attend night school, though he spent the night school tuition on marijuana instead. "Mum, I'm going to quit high school. I'm not going to graduate. That, as you might guess, did not go over well with the English teacher."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 1

xref.title: Duration and Breakup
xref.body: Dane Bramage lasted for almost two years but ultimately ended when Dave Grohl left the band abruptly to join Scream, an opportunity he found irresistible, causing hard feelings among the remaining members. "This band lasted almost two years, but then Dave got a chance to do something else, and he jumped at it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 1

xref.title: Early "Tweey" Sound Transition to Acid House
xref.body: Early in their career, Primal Scream had a distinct "tweey" sound, as exemplified by an 82-second track on the *C86* cassette. This sound defined their formative years before they ventured into acid house music and underwent a significant stylistic shift, eventually becoming known as a "very druggy band." "Primal scream in the years before they discovered acid house and change their sound."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Twee Pop: A History

xref.title: Early Musical Development
xref.body: Dave Grohl began making music in his teens, progressing through a series of short-lived bands that were crucial to his development before joining Scream, then Nirvana, and eventually forming Foo Fighters. These early groups included Freak Baby, Fast, and Dane Bramage, as well as Mishmash Impossible, which notably opened for DC's Fugazi. "A Mishmash of short live bands that went nowhere but were very important to Dave's development."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Before They Were Famous

xref.title: First Object of "Girl Screaming" Affection
xref.body: In the 1920s, Rudy Vallée was identified as the initial male singer who caused female fans to scream hysterically at his performances. This phenomenon of screaming fans would later be seen with artists like Frank Sinatra and The Beatles. "The first object of affection was Rudy Valley back in the 1920s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The More Things Change Part 2

xref.title: First Touring Experiences (Scream)
xref.body: Touring America and Europe (including Amsterdam) with Scream at age 17 or 18 marked his first significant travels beyond Chicago. He cherished these experiences, seeing them as freedom and a clear path to his musical passion, despite the lack of money or large audiences. "And then to Europe for the first time. And wow, I'm an Amsterdam, and I'm 18, and I'm free, man. It was cool. It was great."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 1

xref.title: Influence of Arthur Janov's Primal Scream Therapy
xref.body: Roland Orzabal was deeply interested in psychology and psychiatry at the time, particularly fascinated by the teachings of Arthur Janov, the developer of primal scream therapy. This therapeutic approach encourages patients to delve deep into their psyches to uncover the root of their issues, and was also embraced by figures like John Lennon and Yoko Ono. "Roland was deep into psychology and psychiatry at the time. He was particularly fascinated by the teachings of Arthur Janov, the guy behind primal screen therapy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 9 Great Alt-Rock Cover Songs

xref.title: Influence on Soundgarden Reunion
xref.body: The "critical and commercial disaster" of Chris Cornell's *Scream* album is questioned if it contributed to the Soundgarden reunion the following year. "And you have to wonder how the critical and commercial disaster of the scream album eventually played into the, it'll never happen in our lifetime, Sound Garden reunion the following year."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Spectacular Acts of Self Sabotage

xref.title: Lack of Record Company Intervention
xref.body: During the production of the *Scream* album, there was no one from the record company to tell Chris Cornell that an R&B pop album was "a bad idea" or "off-brand," leading to the album's commercial and critical failure. "But there was no one to tell Chris no."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Spectacular Acts of Self Sabotage

xref.title: Layne Staley's Vocal Style
xref.body: Layne Staley's voice and his harmonies with Jerry Cantrell were central to the band's sound, considered the best hard rock harmonies since David Lee Roth and Michael Anthony in Van Halen's early days. Their vocal arrangements often featured dual lead vocals, strategically overlapped, with the two voices typically separated by a major third. Staley, with the more powerful delivery, could transition from a menacing monotone to sharp, cutting explosions, and also had a great scream, appealing to both metal and alternative fans. "Technically, the two voices were separated by a major third with Lane having the more powerful of the two deliveries."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Groups That Changed Their Front-Person and Survived

xref.title: Lux Interior's Screaming Role
xref.body: Lux interior, the singer for The Cramps, was later hired specifically for his unique ability to scream. His screaming can be heard in Francis Ford Coppola's film version of "Dracula," attributed to Lux rather than actor Gary Oldman. "In fact, singer Lux interior would later be hired for his ability to scream. If you've ever seen Francis Ford Coppola's version of Dracula, that's not Gary Oldham doing the screaming. That's Lux."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Couples in Music

xref.title: Martin Duffy's Death
xref.body: Martin Duffy, who was the keyboardist with Primal Scream, passed away just before Christmas at the age of 55. "And Martin Duffy, keyboardist with primal scream."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022

xref.title: Ministry/Butthole Surfers Collaboration Recording
xref.body: Al Jourgensen recorded a song with Gibby Haynes of the Butthole Surfers, a process complicated by Haynes being extremely high throughout the entire session. Haynes was only capable of screaming through a megaphone and eventually fell off his stool. Jourgensen dedicated two weeks to meticulously editing all of Haynes's vocal tracks to create usable material for the song. "Gibby was so high the entire time that the only thing he could do is scream stuff through a megaphone and then he fell off his stool."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Musicians Who Lost It: Part 2

xref.title: Passenger's Frustration During "Acquiesce" Creation
xref.body: While Noel Gallagher was stuck in the Severant Tunnel and continuously strumming the opening chords of what would become "Acquiesce," a fellow passenger eventually screamed, "The Amine mate. We've heard enough of the guitar now." "something that eventually prompted one of the passengers to scream, the Amine mate. We've heard enough of the guitar now."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In the Studio with Oasis

xref.title: Primal Scream's Reaction to Depeche Mode Tour Decadence
xref.body: Dave Gahan reportedly insisted that Primal Scream open for Depeche Mode on the Devotional Tour because he knew they enjoyed partying. However, Primal Scream was so appalled by the level of drug use and excess they witnessed that they allegedly gave up drugs entirely, despite their prior extensive use. "The story goes that primal scream was so shocked by what they saw that they gave up drugs entirely."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

xref.title: Profound Influence on Multiple Genres
xref.body: PiL had a significant impact on several music genres, including industrial and punk funk. Bands such as Nine Inch Nails, Massive Attack, Manic Street Preachers, Ministry, and Primal Scream have acknowledged PiL's importance. "He hung out with some funk musicians, and eventually pulled together a band that ended up having a profound effect on several genres of music, including industrial and punk funk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 2

xref.title: Quit School at 17
xref.body: Dave Grohl made the decision to quit school at the age of 17 to join the Washington D.C.-based band Scream. This early career move marked his full commitment to music. "Dave quit school at age 17 to join a DC band called Scream."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 2

xref.title: Reni and Mani's Formation and Departure
xref.body: Reni, whose full name is Alan John Wren, joined the band as drummer in 1985. Mani, whose real name is Gary Mounfield, joined as bassist in 1987. They created rock grooves that aligned with the acid house sensibilities of the day. Reni was the first to leave the band in the 1990s as it disintegrated, largely remaining out of sight since, with rumors suggesting he switched to guitar for solo material. Mani later joined Primal Scream. "Rennie was the first guy to leave the band when things began to disintegrate in the 1990s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rhythm Sections

xref.title: Reunion Post-Scream Album
xref.body: Soundgarden reunited the year after Chris Cornell's critically and commercially disastrous *Scream* album, despite previous expectations that a reunion would "never happen in our lifetime." "it'll never happen in our lifetime, Sound Garden reunion the following year."

xref.title: Rich Career Output
xref.body: Fans of Blind Melon fiercely object to the band being labeled a one-hit wonder based on "No Rain," passionately arguing that the band recorded many other excellent songs during their relatively short career, demonstrating a broader musical impact. "They will scream about how many good songs the band recorded during their short career."

xref.title: Singing Lead in Scream
xref.body: He sang lead vocals on the song "God's Look Down" for Scream's fifth album, *Fumble*, despite feeling "totally vulnerable," "naked," and "exposed" when singing lead, preferring the anonymity of a drummer. "I just always felt really weird about singing, like I didn't mind singing backups, but when it's my voice out front, that's when it gets creepy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 1

xref.title: Small Town Perspective on Life and Music
xref.body: Trent Reznor articulated his experience growing up in small-town America, noting a limited scope of travel and the uniformity of amenities like Kmarts and movie theaters showing the same five Sylvester Stallone films. He felt playing music wasn't considered "cool" and that being in the band rather than the football team made you a "leper." "My scope of travel was maybe a half hour radius, and every town had the same Kmart and synoplex, all playing the same five movies, all Sylvester Stallone. It's hard for people who grow up in cities to understand that, to have an endless cornfield in your backyard. But that's what a lot of America is. It's not dodging gunfire from gangs. It wasn't cool to play music where I was, and I got a pretty bad education because I had a bad attitude. If I wanted to get good grades, I could. Stuff I'd like to know now, at the time, I thought was irrelevant. Typical teenage stupidity. I hated school. The fact that it revolved around something you didn't have access to. If you weren't on the football team and you were in the band, you were a leper. When people say those are the best years of our lives, I want to scream. But my parents allowed me to do things that my friends weren't allowed to do."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Big Bands from Small Towns

xref.title: Successor to Scream
xref.body: Dave Grohl joined Nirvana after his tenure with Scream, a move that predated the release of Scream's final album, *Fumble*, by almost three years. "almost three years after Dave joined Nirvana."

xref.title: Title and Name Confusion
xref.body: The various changes imposed by the American label, particularly the reversal of the song title, created confusion, with the song known differently (e.g., "Birds Fly Whisper to a Scream" vs. "Whisper to a Scream Birds Fly") depending on the region. "Maybe all this confusion was why it was a one-hit wonder."
